ports.name: clk_i
ports.functionality: Supplies the rising edge timing for the entity's clocked processes; it sequences updates to lock_q and bus_rsp_o on rising edges. It is the process clock for both spinlock and response logic.
ports.evidence: rising_edge(clk_i) used in both spinlock and bus_response processes to update lock_q and bus_rsp_o.

ports.name: rstn_i
ports.functionality: When low it resets lock_q bits and the bus_rsp_o response record; it is tested in the reset branch of the clocked processes to initialize state. It overrides normal updates during reset.
ports.evidence: if (rstn_i = '0') then branches in spinlock and bus_response processes set lock_q and bus_rsp_o to initial values.

ports.name: bus_req_i
ports.functionality: Record carrying bus request fields; the aggregate itself is not used as a whole in this source, its individual fields are read and acted upon instead.
ports.evidence: Only bus_req_i's fields (addr, stb, rw, etc.) are referenced in comparisons and assignments; no whole-record use appears.

ports.name: bus_req_i.addr
ports.functionality: Supplies address bits used to decode which spinlock index is selected (addr(6 downto 2)) and to choose between masked or full responses (addr(7)). It therefore selects sel bits and gates lock/read behavior.
ports.evidence: sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = to_unsigned(i,5)) else '0'; if (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') then branches in processes.

ports.name: bus_req_i.data
ports.functionality: Declared data field of the bus request but not referenced anywhere in this source; no logic reads or forwards it here.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.data in the processes or concurrent statements.

ports.name: bus_req_i.ben
ports.functionality: Declared byte-enable field but not read or used in this entity's source; no logic depends on it here.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.ben does not appear in any assignment, condition or expression.

ports.name: bus_req_i.stb
ports.functionality: Acts as the bus transaction enable: when '1' it enables lock updates and response generation; its value is also captured into bus_rsp_o.ack on the next clock edge.
ports.evidence: Condition (bus_req_i.stb = '1') guards lock_q update and data-response assignments; bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb in bus_response process.

ports.name: bus_req_i.rw
ports.functionality: Supplies the read/write bit used to set a lock bit (lock_q <= not bus_req_i.rw) and is tested to enable read-response data generation (rw = '0').
ports.evidence: lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw assigned in spinlock process; bus_response tests (bus_req_i.rw = '0') to drive data output.

ports.name: bus_req_i.src
ports.functionality: Declared source field of the request but not used anywhere in this entity's source; no logic reads it.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.src is not referenced in assignments or conditions.

ports.name: bus_req_i.priv
ports.functionality: Declared privilege indicator but not referenced in this source; the entity does not consume or forward it here.
ports.evidence: No occurrences of bus_req_i.priv in the code.

ports.name: bus_req_i.debug
ports.functionality: Declared debug flag but unused in the entity's logic; it is neither tested nor forwarded here.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.debug does not appear in any condition or assignment.

ports.name: bus_req_i.amo
ports.functionality: Declared AMO flag but not referenced in this source; the entity ignores it.
ports.evidence: No usage of bus_req_i.amo in the provided code.

ports.name: bus_req_i.amoop
ports.functionality: Declared AMO operation bits but not read or used here; the entity's logic does not reference them.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.amoop is not present in any expression or assignment.

ports.name: bus_req_i.lock
ports.functionality: Declared lock control bit but not used in this source; lock control is implemented from addr/rw/stb rather than this field here.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.lock is not referenced in the processes or concurrent assignment.

ports.name: bus_req_i.fence
ports.functionality: Declared fence flag but not referenced in this entity; no logic consumes it here.
ports.evidence: bus_req_i.fence is absent from all conditions and assignments.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o
ports.functionality: Constructs and presents the response record to the outside: its fields are produced in the clocked bus_response process from bus_req_i.stb, constants, and lock_q/sel and then exported off-chip.
ports.evidence: bus_response process assigns bus_rsp_o fields from bus_req_i.stb, constants and lock_q/sel and the record is output from the entity.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.ack
ports.functionality: Captured from bus_req_i.stb on the rising clock edge and presented as the ack output; reset is provided by the response reset value in the reset branch.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.ack <= bus_req_i.stb inside the bus_response process on rising_edge(clk_i).

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.err
ports.functionality: Assigned a constant '0' each clock and forwarded to the outside as the err output; it does not depend on any internal declared signal.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.err <= '0' in bus_response process; no declared source supplies its value.

ports.name: bus_rsp_o.data
ports.functionality: Holds the read response data captured each clock: when reading it captures either lock_q masked by sel (addr(7)=0) or the full lock_q (addr(7)=1), and then exports this vector as the response data.
ports.evidence: bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel or bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q inside bus_response process when bus_req_i.rw = '0'.

signals.name: lock_q
signals.functionality: Holds per-bit lock state; each bit is reset to '0' and on a selected transaction (stb and addr(7)=0 and sel(i)=1) captures not bus_req_i.rw, and supplies bits to the response data.
signals.evidence: In spinlock process lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw when stb and addr(7)='0' and sel(i)='1'; bus_response reads lock_q into bus_rsp_o.data.

signals.name: sel
signals.functionality: Combinationally derives which lock index is selected from bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) and supplies per-bit selection that gates lock updates and masks the response data when requested.
signals.evidence: sel(i) <= '1' when (bus_req_i.addr(6 downto 2) = to_unsigned(i,5)) else '0'; sel(i) used in spinlock condition and in bus_rsp_o.data <= lock_q and sel.
